more.accuracyBody: How close we are to the reference
device.title: Device
device.actions.hrBody: The standard Bluetooth heart rate service lets gym equipment and other apps read your heart rate. The band keeps this setting after a restart. Turning it off also stops live heart rate in OpenHoop.
device.actions.hrUnknown: Not changed from OpenHoop. The band does not report the current setting.
device.firmwareBody: Firmware updates can change the data format. This app never updates firmware.
device.flags.title: Feature flags
device.flags.levelD: Level D: configuration as read from the band. On is 1 and off is 2, as the band reports them.
device.pack.title: Battery pack
device.pack.body: When a battery pack charges the band, the band passes on what the pack reports. OpenHoop shows the last report from a sync. Reading the pack is experimental.
device.status.title: Band status
device.status.body: From the band's own reports at the last sync.
device.info.title: Band info
device.pack.empty.title: No battery pack report yet
device.pack.empty.body: The band reports a pack only while one is attached and charging it. Attach it, then sync. Until then nothing is shown or estimated.
device.safety.title: Safety lock
device.safety.howBody: The button turns on once the code is typed, so a dangerous command can never go out with one tap.
appSettings.title: App settings
appSettings.themeBody: System follows your phone's light or dark setting.
appSettings.syncProblemsBody: When a sync fails, or the band has not synced for {days} days
appSettings.integrations.healthConnectBo: Writes heart rate, sleep and SpO₂. Reads weight and steps. Never scores.
appSettings.integrations.importFileBody: Past scores, also used for the accuracy report
appSettings.provider.title: Providers
appSettings.provider.partnerBody: They rely on a partner's servers or staff, so OpenHoop does not offer them.
appSettings.provider.consent: A provider would only see what you approve, per data type, and you could revoke it at any time.
privacy.title: Data & privacy
privacy.importExportBody: Back up your data or bring a file in
privacy.import.useBody: Comparing past scores night by night, and keeping history from before OpenHoop clearly labelled and separate from ours.
privacy.import.localBody: The file is read on this phone. Nothing is uploaded, and OpenHoop never contacts the official app's servers or your account there.
dev.title: Developer
dev.introBody: Nothing here changes your data or the band.
dev.selftestBody: Encryption and pipeline checks on this device
dev.statesBody: Examples of every empty and error state
aboutx.accuracyLink: Read how the levels are assigned
aboutx.support.freeBody: Every feature is free. Donations help pay for test bands and reference devices.
aboutx.support.customAmountError: That amount cannot be used. Enter whole dollars, from $1 to $12,000.
aboutx.support.donateNote: The GitHub Sponsors checkout opens in a sheet over the app with your amount filled in, and closing it brings you back. You pay by card in US dollars and need a GitHub account. GitHub takes no fee on sponsorships from personal accounts.
aboutx.support.openFailed: GitHub could not be opened. Check that a web browser is installed and try again.
aboutx.accuracy.title: Accuracy
aboutx.accuracy.body: Each value also has a level that says how it is produced.
community.teamsBody: OpenHoop is local-first, so there are no teams by default. Sharing is planned as opt-in.
community.selfHostBody: Plug-in, you choose what is shared
community.ownBody: A teams plug-in would only see the scores you pick, per team.
states.notConnected.title: Band not connected
states.notConnected.body: Bring it close and make sure Bluetooth is on.
states.syncing.title: Syncing with the band
states.syncing.body: You can keep using the app.
states.lowBattery.title: Low band battery
states.charging.title: Charging
states.charging.body: The band is charging. Tracking pauses while it is off your wrist.
states.calibrating.title: Calibrating: {count} nights left
states.calibrating.body: Scores appear once we know your normal.
states.noData.title: No data for this day
states.noData.body: The band was not worn. Nothing to show, and no guesses.
states.needsMg.title: Needs MG hardware
states.needsMg.body: ECG and blood pressure research need a WHOOP MG band.
states.offline.title: Offline
states.offline.body: Nothing needs the internet. Your data is safe on this phone.
states.dataAtRisk.title: Data at risk
states.dataAtRisk.body: No sync for {days} days. The band overwrites its history after about 20 days.
states.firstDay.title: First day
states.firstDay.body: Wear your band tonight. Your first scores arrive tomorrow morning.
states.waitingForData.title: Band paired, no data yet
states.waitingForData.body: Wear your band tonight and sync tomorrow morning. Your first scores need a full night.
states.gallery.title: System states
states.gallery.intro: Developer mode: examples of the states the app shows when there is nothing to show. The numbers are placeholders.
appSettings.notificationsAllowBody: Your phone asks for permission when you turn this on.
appSettings.notificationsBlocked: Notifications are blocked for OpenHoop in your phone settings. Allow them there first.
appSettings.quietInvalid: Not a valid time. Use HH:MM.
appSettings.notificationsLocal: Notifications are scheduled on this phone only. There is no server and no push service. The digest arrives at 07:00, or when your quiet hours end.
bandConfig.source.demo: These values come from the simulated band, not from a real WHOOP.
bandConfig.source.band: These values were read from your band.
bandConfig.unverifiedNote: Reading and changing these values was checked on an MG band (firmware 50.43.2.0). The key names come from the band and a reference project; the readable names are plain renderings of the key names, not confirmed meanings.
bandConfig.missing.title: Not read yet
bandConfig.missing.body: The configuration of this band has not been read. Read it to store a snapshot on this phone.
bandConfig.malformed.title: Could not read
bandConfig.malformed.body: The stored snapshot is damaged, so nothing is shown. Read the configuration again.
bandConfig.empty.title: No fields returned
bandConfig.empty.body: The stored snapshot holds no flags or settings. A locked band may not answer these commands.
bandConfig.otherBody: OpenHoop does not know these fields. They are shown exactly as the band returned them.
bandConfig.write.title: Changing a setting
bandConfig.write.body: A change is written to the band's memory and stays after a restart. Only the values 1 and 2 (on and off) can be changed, because only those can be put back. OpenHoop keeps the old value and offers to put it back. Some settings change how the band measures, so change only what you understand.
bandConfig.write.dialogBody: This writes {to} to {key} (now {from}) in the band's memory. It stays after a restart until you put it back. Type {word} to continue.
error.bandConfigBusy: A sync or live heart rate is running. Wait until it finishes, then read the configuration.
error.bandConfigEmpty: The band returned no flags or settings, so nothing was stored. A locked band may not answer.
error.streamsBusy: An ECG reading or a sync is running. Wait until it finishes and try again.
error.ecgStreamsOn: Raw optical or motion data is streaming. Switch it off in Developer, or finish the workout, and try again.
error.syncStreamsOn: Raw optical or motion data is streaming in Developer. Switch it off and sync again.
error.streamRefused: The band refused the raw data stream.
error.bandBusy: A sync or live heart rate is running. Wait until it finishes and try again.
error.configNotWritable: This value could not be put back once changed, so OpenHoop does not change it.
error.configNotApplied: The band did not keep the new value. Nothing else was changed.
error.configNoChange: OpenHoop has no earlier value for this setting.
bandConfig.config.whoop_live_hr_in_adv_i: Live heart rate in advertising packet
import.how.title: Get your export from the official app
import.how.body: Ask the official app for your data export (look for a data export or download my data option in its settings). It sends you a ZIP file with CSV files. Save it on this phone, then choose it here. OpenHoop never logs in to the official app for you.
import.formats: Choose the ZIP as it arrived, or its CSV files: physiological cycles, sleeps, workouts and journal entries. Files over 25 MB are refused.
import.result.title: Import finished
import.result.legend: Skipped rows were already imported, repeated in the file or had no values. Invalid rows had a time or a value that could not be trusted.
import.problem.unrecognised: not recognised as part of the official export
import.problem.csv-limits: is too large or too wide to read
import.problem.unsupported: is not a ZIP or CSV file
import.problem.zip-limits: holds too many files or too much data
import.stored.title: From the official app's export
import.stored.note: These are the official app's own numbers, as it exported them. OpenHoop did not compute or change them. They stay apart from your band data and from OpenHoop's own scores.
import.stored.empty: Nothing imported yet. Values you import show up here, labelled as the official app's.
import.chart.title: Recovery from the official app
import.chart.empty: No recovery values in the import
import.history.title: Imported history
import.history.empty: Nothing of this kind was imported.
import.remove.confirm: Remove {count} imported rows from this phone? Your band data and OpenHoop's own scores are not touched.
import.chart.note: Shows up to the latest {count} cycles that have a recovery value.
import.result.already: Already up to date: these rows were imported before
appSettings.integrations.othersNotBuilt: Other online services and the providers on the next screen need a partner server, so they are not part of OpenHoop. Strava is the one online service, and it only sends what you upload yourself.
hc.androidOnlyBody: Health Connect is part of Android. On this phone OpenHoop keeps your data to itself.
hc.notInstalledBody: Install it from the Play Store to share data with other health apps on this phone.
hc.updateRequiredBody: Update it in the Play Store, then come back here.
hc.intro: Health Connect is Android's shared store for health data on this phone. Nothing leaves the phone, but apps you allow in Health Connect can read what OpenHoop writes there. Every type stays off until you turn it on.
hc.type.sleepBody: Start and end, with naps and your corrections. No sleep stages.
hc.type.nightlyBody: One value per night, at wake time
hc.type.weightBody: Added to your body log with the app it came from. Your own entries are never overwritten.
hc.type.bodyFatBody: Only with a weight from the same app and day
hc.type.stepsBody: Only for days without steps from the band. A day with band steps always keeps the band value. Turning this off removes the copied steps from OpenHoop.
hc.window: OpenHoop writes the last {days} days and replaces only what it wrote itself. Data from other apps is never changed.
hc.afterSyncBody: Otherwise only when you tap Sync now
hc.demoNote: The demo band is the data source. Its data is simulated, so OpenHoop writes none of it to Health Connect. Reading weight still works.
hc.manageBody: Turning a type off here stops syncing it. To withdraw a permission or delete what OpenHoop wrote, use Health Connect.
hc.result.store: Could not save on this phone
aboutx.donateData.title: Donate your data
aboutx.donateData.rowBody: Share raw band data and official values to improve accuracy
aboutx.donateData.intro: Help make OpenHoop more accurate. Choose days, and the app packs the raw band data with the official values for those days. You then post the files yourself in a public GitHub issue.
aboutx.donateData.goesIn: Goes in: raw band records, the official values you imported, and OpenHoop's own results for those days.
aboutx.donateData.staysOut: Stays out: your name and profile, the serial number, Bluetooth address and name of the band and of its battery pack, band log lines that mention them, journal, notes, GPS, coach chats and cycle tracking.
aboutx.donateData.realDates: Dates and times stay real. You need a free GitHub account.
aboutx.donateData.demo: Demo data cannot be donated. Connect your band first.
aboutx.donateData.empty: No finished day has raw band data yet. Sync your band and come back tomorrow.
aboutx.donateData.importBody: Days with official values are the most useful.
aboutx.donateData.consent: I understand this becomes public on GitHub, under my account, cannot be taken back, and is shared under CC0 1.0: anyone may use it for anything.
aboutx.donateData.consentRange: I understand that {n} days, from {from} to {to}, become public on GitHub, under my account, cannot be taken back, and are shared under CC0 1.0: anyone may use them for anything.
aboutx.donateData.savedOne: 1 file is in your folder. Attach it to the post, then submit.
aboutx.donateData.savedMany: {n} files are in your folder. Attach all {n} to the post, then submit.
aboutx.donateData.savedMore: You can attach the rest in comments on the same issue after posting.
aboutx.donateData.skipped: Left out because they had no band data: {days}
aboutx.donateData.shareEachBody: The folder could not be used, so save each file yourself, then open GitHub.
aboutx.donateData.pickCancelled: No folder was chosen. The files are ready.
aboutx.donateData.errorEmpty: None of the chosen days still has raw band data.
aboutx.donateData.errorBuild: The files could not be made. Check that there is enough free space and try again.
aboutx.donateData.githubFailed: GitHub could not be opened. The files are in your folder; post them at github.com/DarioDML/OpenHoop/issues.
aboutx.donateData.folderHint: After you tap Donate, choose a folder for the files. On Android, Download itself cannot be chosen: create one inside it, for example OpenHoop.
more.helpBody: What every term and level means
device.tile.batteryMissing: Unknown until the band is read
device.tile.healthCaption: The band does not share how worn its battery is.
device.wear.title: Wear location
device.wear.sheetBody: Where you wear the band. OpenHoop keeps it as a note; scores do not change with it yet.
device.configNotRead: Not read from the band yet
device.findBody: Buzzes for longer so you can hear it. Tap stop to end early.
device.rangeNote: The band has to be in Bluetooth range.
device.broadcastBody: Standard BLE profile for Zwift, Peloton, Strava
device.motionCaption: Streams the band's motion while a strength session is open in the app, for reps, time under tension and muscular load. Uses band battery while it runs.
device.motionBody: Costs battery. Needed for muscular load
device.dangerNote: OpenHoop cannot wipe, restart or unpair a band yet. When it can, each of these will need the last characters of the serial number typed to confirm.
appSettings.goalHitsBody: When you reach your steps goal or a weekly plan goal
appSettings.coachCheckinsBody: Max 1 a day, in the evening
appSettings.coachCheckinsOff: Turn on the coach under Data & privacy first
appSettings.restoreLayoutNone: There is no earlier layout to go back to
notif.goalHit.title: Goal hit
notif.coach.title: Coach check-in
notif.coach.body: How did today go? Open the coach to talk it through.
appSettings.integrations.scaleIos: Needs Apple Health, which is not built yet
strava.autoShare.title: Strava auto-share
strava.autoShare.body: Shares activities that start after you turn this on, 15 minutes after they end. Heart rate and route go with them, with the start and end of the route hidden if you chose that.
strava.autoShare.manualBody: Nothing is sent by itself. Share an activity from its details page.
strava.autoShare.needsConnection: Connect Strava and turn on its network feature first. Until then nothing is shared.
privacy.hero.localBody: No network traffic. Encrypted on this phone.
privacy.hero.networkBody: Only the features you switched on below talk to the internet. Everything else stays on this phone, encrypted.
privacy.backupBody: Not built: OpenHoop has no accounts or cloud storage. Export below to keep a copy yourself.
privacy.retentionBody: Raw records are the band's bytes as received. After each sync, raw records older than this are removed. Per-second readings, scores and everything you entered stay.
privacy.retentionConfirmBody: Raw records older than {days} days are removed now and after every sync. They cannot be decoded again later or donated. Readings and scores stay.
privacy.export.csvBody: Per-second vitals and daily scores, one file per table
privacy.export.jsonBody: Every table as JSON, workouts with heart rate and GPS included
privacy.export.databaseBody: SQLite copy. Not encrypted, so keep it safe.
privacy.networkOffNote: Turn off local-only mode above to use these.
privacy.deleteAllBody: Deletes every reading, score, journal entry, setting, import and saved raw session stored by OpenHoop on this phone, including the band configuration saved before OpenHoop changed it, so those changes can no longer be put back in one tap. An alarm on the band is cancelled when the band is connected; otherwise it stays set on the band. Strava stays connected and the coach key stays saved until you remove them on their own screens.
privacy.deleteAllDialog: This cannot be undone. The saved original band configuration is deleted too, so OpenHoop can no longer put back what it changed on the band. Export first if you want a copy. Type {word} to confirm.
error.exportDatabase: The database copy could not be made, so nothing was shared. Try the CSV export instead.
dev.packetsEmpty: No packets yet. They appear while the band talks to the phone, for example during a sync or live heart rate.
dev.packetsNote: Logged only while this screen is open or a recording runs. Kept in memory and never saved, unless you record.
dev.recordBody: Saves every packet to a CSV file on this phone. Saved sessions go into the data export.
dev.recordFailed: The session could not be saved.
dev.stream.ppgBody: Raw optical channels from the band's LEDs, about 25 Hz. Stops after 10 minutes or when you leave this tab.
dev.stream.imuBody: Raw acceleration and rotation, 100 Hz. Stops after 10 minutes or when you leave this tab.
dev.stream.tempBody: 1 Hz, inside every history record. There is no separate stream to switch.
dev.channel.why.pulse: This channel carries the strongest pulse at a medium LED drive. That fits a green LED, but the band does not say which colour it uses.
dev.channel.why.wear: A low LED drive with a high baseline and a weak pulse. That fits the infrared light the band uses to check it is on your wrist.
dev.channel.why.dark: Every LED is off here, so the detector only sees ambient light. It is the baseline the other channels are compared with.
dev.channel.why.spo2Red: Used in the band's own SpO2 windows during sleep. Its colour is inferred, not read from the band.
dev.channel.why.spo2Ir: Used in the band's own SpO2 windows during sleep. Its colour is inferred, not read from the band.
dev.channel.why.unknown: An LED and detector pair OpenHoop has not seen before.
dev.channel.note: Raw counts, last 5 s. Red and IR for SpO2 light up only in the band's own sleep windows.
dev.recordStreamsBody: Saves one CSV per stream, with units: motion in g and °/s, optical in raw counts with LED, detector and drive. Saved files are listed under Packets.
dev.recordStreamsFailed: The CSV files could not be saved.
dev.streamsLevel: Raw band data. Channel colours are inferred from LED drive and pulse strength, not read from the band.
aboutx.affiliationBody: This is an independent open-source project. WHOOP is a trademark of its owner. It talks to bands you own, for interoperability.
aboutx.accuracy.summaryNone: Not measured on your data yet
aboutx.accuracy.noneBody: Import an export from the official app. OpenHoop then compares its own values with the official ones, night by night, on this phone.
aboutx.accuracy.turnedOff: Using imported data for this report is turned off on the import page.
aboutx.accuracy.footnote: Compared on this phone with the official values you imported. Each number is the average difference per night. Nothing is sent anywhere.
aboutx.accuracy.stagesNote: Sleep stages are checked against a public lab dataset, not your own nights.
bandConfig.title: Configuration
bandConfig.restoreOneBody: This writes {value} back to {key}, the value it had before OpenHoop changed it. Type {word} to continue.
device.safety.question: Unpair this band?
device.safety.sheetBody: Unpairing, wiping or restarting a band cannot be undone.
device.safety.backlog: {count} pages are not synced yet and stay on the band until it overwrites them.
device.safety.serialHint: The last four characters of the serial number.
device.safety.noSerialHint: The serial number is not known yet, so type the word instead.
import.title: Import
import.use.accuracyBody: Compare our scores night by night
import.use.historyBody: Shown with an 'official' label, never mixed with ours
import.use.historyOff: Only days from {day} on are imported.
import.nothingFound: Nothing in this file can be imported. Check that it is the official app's export.
device.pack.chargesEmpty: No charging was recorded in the last 30 days.
device.pack.chargesNote: Counted from the band's own charging events.
device.pack.cyclesCaption: The pack does not share its cycle count.
device.pack.levelNote: The pack's own values as the band passes them on. No estimates.
appSettings.provider.heroBody: They rely on servers or people. Plug one in, or skip.
appSettings.provider.pluginBody: Plug-ins for partners and a self-hosted teams server are not built. OpenHoop has no accounts and no server, so nothing can be plugged in yet.
appSettings.provider.teamsNotBuilt: Teams and leaderboards need a self-hosted server, which is not built yet.
states.gallery.heading: Honest when there's nothing to show
device.safety.nothingSent: This version of OpenHoop cannot unpair, wipe or restart a band. Typing the code shows how the lock will work; confirming changes nothing on the band.
bandConfig.changesExplained: Counts the {total} values OpenHoop can change, compared with what the band had before OpenHoop first changed one.
bandConfig.putBackNone: OpenHoop has not changed any value on this band.
bandConfig.putBackBody: This writes the earlier value back to {keys}, one key at a time. If one write fails, the ones after it are not sent. Type {word} to continue.
bandConfig.putBackPartial: Put back {restored} of {total}. The rest still have the value OpenHoop wrote.
import.use.historyNoStart: No worn-since date is set yet, so everything in the file is imported. Set the date under Data & privacy to import only days from then on.
dev.exportSessionsNote: Shares only the saved session files, without the database. The files hold the raw bytes the band sent.
dev.recordFull: The recording is full at {limit} packets. Stop it to save what it holds.
dev.recordLeave: Leaving this screen stops the recording and saves it.
